_readme: Single source of truth for the worker's wire vocabulary: the notification-type tokens the platform persists inside notification envelopes (the Go agent package's NotificationType* constants and the browser's NOTIFICATION_TYPE are generated from this file), the notification-thread wrapper discriminator, the one Codex rateLimitReachedType that lifts on a timer, and the model sentinels. workerWrittenNotificationTypes lists the types the WORKER is the sole writer of -- the browser keeps a standalone-row set from it, and a type moves between the two regimes by editing this file, not by editing a per-side list. Adding a notification type is: one entry here, task generate, and both sides' dispatch switches compile against it. GoalUpdated/GoalCleared are worker-written on purpose: five providers report a session goal in five different wire shapes, and persisting each verbatim would put every provider's goal parsing in that provider's renderer. The worker normalizes once and writes a neutral row, so the browser has ONE goal renderer. goalStatusTokens and goalTransitions are the session goal's two payload vocabularies. The worker writes both inside the goal_updated notification -- goal_status is the neutral status the row stores, goal_transition is what the change DID -- and notificationRenderers reads both to build the transcript line. Both were hand-written on the two sides before this contract existed, and the status tokens are ALSO the SQL CHECK list on agents.goal_status, which the generator cannot emit; keep that third spelling in step by hand. goal_transition is a separate vocabulary from the status because several different changes land on one status: a resume and a first set both end `active`, and only the applier, which holds the row from before the write, can tell them apart. Every token here has a producer in goalTransitionKind; a token nothing writes is a label the browser can never render, so add one only with the branch that emits it. AgentStatus is worker-written for the same reason the goal pair is: a provider states a live status in its own shape -- Goose sends a `status_message` notice, Reasonix a session phase -- and persisting each verbatim would put that parsing in that provider's renderer. The worker normalizes once, so the browser has ONE status row. It carries `text` alone, because a status IS a sentence. `notificationFields` holds every payload key the worker writes onto a notification and the browser reads back, `type` and `label` among them: the envelope discriminator was hand-spelled at 31 Go writers beside a generated NotificationType* value, and `label` sits in the settings_changed entry beside `old_label` and `new_label`, which already came from here. Every value is snake_case, and the schema refuses anything else: this table CHOOSES the wire key and the Go struct tags follow it, so a new entry cannot pick its own convention. The goal family is the reason it is not two entries: the worker's own comment at output_goal.go says `goal_transition` exists so a RESUMED goal does not announce itself as a new one, and a rename of that key alone restores exactly that regression.
